- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion to prevent overextension.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d, net supply negative), model overestimates bullishness — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% relative to historical mean of same event density.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misread trend direction — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth out short-term noise.
- When official events are clustered (e.g., multiple auctions in 3–5 days), model often fails to account for event clustering — reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to reflect event-induced noise dampening.
- In low-sentiment, high-supply environments, model tends to ignore bearish sentiment — force a downward bias adjustment if sentiment < 0.25 and supply net < -15.00.
